name: Tsukiyo no Mura
source:
A young magazine journalist returned to the village where he spent his childhood, accompanied by his female assistant, for a story.
What awaited him was the same oppressive, stifling atmosphere he remembered from his youth—and a childhood friend who had grown into a stunningly beautiful young woman.
This woman, who now used her body to dominate the men of the village, sought to draw the two of them into the village’s insular, suffocating circle.

The Moon Women
In this village, women who exhibited strange behavior from time to time were said to be possessed by foxes.
The men called these women kitsune-tsuki (fox-possessed) and took it upon themselves to "manage" them.
Under the guise of exorcising the foxes, the men would violate these women.
Over time, the term kitsune-tsuki gradually shifted to tsuki-onna (possessed women).
Since the men would visit these women at night, in a village with no streetlights, the moonlight became their guide.
And so, the tsuki(possessed)-onna  came to be known as tsuki(moon)-onna—Moon Women.

translation:
一名年輕雜誌記者帶著女助手回到童年生活過的村莊，準備撰寫報導。
等待他的，是記憶中壓抑、窒息的氛圍，以及一位已經長成美麗年輕女子的青梅竹馬。
如今，這名女人用身體支配村裡的男人，試圖把他們兩人拖入村莊封閉而令人窒息的圈子。

月女
這個村莊裡，偶爾表現出奇怪行為的女性被認為是被狐狸附身。
男人稱她們為「狐附身」，並負責「管理」她們。
他們以驅逐狐狸為名侵犯這些女性。
隨著時間推移，「狐附身」一詞逐漸變成「附身女人」。
由於男人會在夜晚拜訪這些女人，而村裡沒有街燈，月光成了他們的嚮導。
因此，附身女人最終被稱為月女。
